item.title: ShipStation Deploys Deckhand AI Agent for Slack Help Desk on Amazon Bedrock
item.description:
ShipStation Deploys Deckhand AI Agent for Slack Help Desk on Amazon Bedrock

ShipStation Global Engineering launched Deckhand, an AI‑powered IT help‑desk agent that lives in Slack and runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

🔍 Overview

  • Repetitive IT questions, error‑message screenshots, and off‑hours tickets consumed time that could be spent elsewhere.
  • Knowledge was scattered across Confluence articles, intranet pages, PDFs, IT‑maintained guides, and the Slack channel history.
  • In the 12 months before launch employees posted more than 1,500 threads, with over a fifth of questions arriving outside US business hours.
  • Deckhand resolves 97.5 % of incoming channel queries and earned a 96 % positive‑feedback rating (Figure 1).

🧩 How it works

  • When an employee posts in a channel where Deckhand is present, the Slack service assembles the full thread history and user context (name, email, time zone, manager).
  • The request is sent to the AgentCore runtime API.
  • The agent searches an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base (indexed content from Confluence, the intranet, Slack, and marketing pages stored in Amazon S3) and calls tools as needed.
  • If the answer is not found, the agent asks a clarifying question or offers to create a Jira Service Management ticket.
Component Description
Slack service FastAPI + Slack Bolt app hosted on AWS App Runner; receives Slack events, builds user‑context payload
Agent service Strands agent deployed as a container on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime; uses Anthropic Claude via Bedrock
Tools & knowledge Single AWS Lambda exposed as Model Context Protocol tools; classifies requests, creates/updates Jira tickets, analyzes images
Knowledge base Amazon S3‑backed index of Confluence, intranet, Slack, and marketing content
Operations Amazon DynamoDB stores feedback; AWS X‑Ray traces request paths; Amazon CloudWatch logs

⚙️ Key details

  • Runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, which hosts the agent in isolated sessions—no servers or containers to manage.
  • Integrates with Jira Service Management to create fully contextualized tickets with one click.
  • Can read error‑message screenshots and respond directly in the Slack conversation.
  • Operates like a teammate: joins channels, reads conversation history, and draws context from Slack profiles.

🚀 Impact

  • Repetitive questions that previously required manual lookup are now answered on the spot.
  • Employees receive help by simply asking a question in Slack, eliminating the need to fill out ticket forms.
  • The IT team is freed from repeatedly saying “please file a ticket,” reducing operational friction.

💡 Why it matters

  • Shows that AI agents can consolidate fragmented knowledge sources and provide instant support for globally distributed teams.
  • Improves employee experience and operational efficiency for a leading intelligent shipping and logistics platform.

#ShipStation #AIAgents #Slack #AmazonBedrock #ITAutomation

Source: How ShipStation Global built an AI IT help desk on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services Source: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Slack introduces AI-powered Slackforce Surfaces for building interactive tools in chat
item.description:
Slack introduces AI-powered Slackforce Surfaces for building interactive tools in chat

Slack is launching a new feature called Slackforce Surfaces that allows users to create interactive reports, dashboards, and other tools directly within a chat using AI.

🧩 How it works

Users can build a tool by describing what they need to Slackbot. The AI then gathers information from connected apps and relevant conversations to create the output.

Key capabilities include the creation of:

  • Interactive reports
  • Polls
  • Dashboards
  • Presentations
  • Microsites

In one example, a user asked Slackbot for an arcade-themed visualization of AI token usage, and the assistant generated an interactive dashboard showing token usage across engineering, design, and sales divisions.

⚙️ Key details

  • Collaboration: Once a Surface is created, it can be pinned to channels and shared with colleagues, who can then interact with it and leave comments.
  • Data Privacy: The feature only pulls information that the user has given its AI tools permission to access.
  • Integration: Slackbot can gather data from connected apps, such as Salesforce or Google Drive.

🚀 Availability

Slackforce Surfaces is available to all customers, including those using the free version, provided Slackbot is enabled in their workspace. Support for live data will begin in October.

#Slack #AI #Productivity #SlackforceSurfaces

Source: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats

item.title: Multiplayer Agent Harness for Collaborative Work in Slack and Web
item.description:
Multiplayer Agent Harness for Collaborative Work in Slack and Web

A new multiplayer agent harness for work has been introduced, enabling employees to work independently in isolated workspaces or collaborate with an agent in projects, group messages, and Slack channels.

🔍 Overview

The system allows users to customize their own agent while maintaining the ability to work collaboratively. Identity and configuration are consistent between the web app and Slack. Key capabilities include:

  • Internal Search: Search across the web, databases, documents, email, and internal notes.
  • Inbox Management: Triage inboxes on a schedule with reply drafts and labels by learning a user’s writing voice from past sends.
  • Development Workflow: Work in existing repositories to monitor CI, run tests, check system logs, and open PRs.
  • Project Tracking: Post follow-ups and updates in shared channels to track projects.
  • App Creation: Build and publish custom internal apps to specific people.

🧩 How it works

Each person and room is provided with its own scoped memory, permissions, files, keychain view, durable sandbox, crons, and web apps.

  • Core Architecture: The core runs TypeScript on Node and uses Fastify for HTTP. A Postgres persistence layer manages session history, user data, and other durable state.
  • Integration: The web UI, public portal, and admin panel are optional plugins over the core’s HTTP API. Slack is an optional in-process plugin supervised through a direct service client.
  • Tooling: The agent uses a small, fixed tool surface. The execute tool allows the agent to run commands in its own isolated, durable sandbox where installed tools remain installed.
  • Tech Stack: The Slack plugin uses Bolt, while the web UI utilizes Vite for builds and Lit for rendering.
  • Vendor Neutrality: The core is driven by Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code, meaning deployments are not tied to a single vendor.

⚙️ Key details

Administrators can set a security posture, org-level configuration, and determine available models and harnesses.

Security Posture Description
Strict Every harness tool call requires human approval, except for two no-effect turn enders.
Auto (default) A classifier screens tool results and provenance-labelled external data; deployments can use their own screening proxy.
Dangerous No pauses between tool calls and no content screening.

Regardless of the posture, a predeclared command policy applies to provide hard denials and approval rules for destructive SQL or recursive deletes.

Additional technical specifications include:

  • Deployment: Every company’s specific configuration, infrastructure, custom tools, skills, and sandbox image live in a deployment directory validated and deployed via the qm CLI. Each deployment runs in the operator’s own cloud account.
  • Skills: Skills are scope-owned and shareable by grant. Skill packs can be imported from git repositories, and admin-gated promotion to the whole org is available.
  • Automation: Inbound webhooks, watches, and crons run work independently.
  • Memory: Built-in notebooks are available, though memory can be routed by scope to external providers.
